evidence.note: Recurring TodoWrite checkpoints from opening to close indicate a sustained running ledger of status, not a one-shot declaration of done.
Full correctness sweeps (full_test.py, mask test, edge cases, big edge cases) show tracking correctness across the shape/distribution/mask grid rather than eyeballing one case.
Targeted probes of specific shapes ('Check 2048 case', 'Check D=768 fail') show awareness of which shapes gate the score / bind the worst case.
'All shapes' and 'Stable bench all shapes' benchmarking captures the max-of-10 latency picture; repeated stability/variability checks show awareness of noisy per-shape medians.
'Verify still working' and post-failure error checks show catching regressions when a change touches correctness — cross-case regression awareness.

Very heavy repeated re-tuning of the same components (bmm/tail/proj_gate) across dozens of steps; ambiguous whether disciplined bottleneck focus or partial circularity, which caps below the top anchor.

reasoning: The agent maintains an explicit todo ledger at multiple checkpoints, sweeps correctness across the grid including mask/edge/specific failing shapes (D=768, 2048), benchmarks all 10 shapes for the worst-case latency, and re-verifies after edits to catch regressions — matching much of the level-8 description. However, I cannot inspect the ledger contents to confirm per-shape/per-distribution granularity, and the very heavy repeated re-tuning of the same components with no observable evidence of detecting stuck/circular states or reallocating away from them keeps it below 8 and well short of 10. This places observed behavior between the 5 and 8 anchors, at 7.
